output.question: Has Paramount announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. As of mid-November 2026, Paramount Skydance's leadership has told staff that layoffs will come with its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, but it has not said how many jobs will go. Co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz warned employees in a memo that combining the companies would involve layoffs, and the company targets more than $6 billion in cost savings within three years. Variety reports, as relayed by Comicbasics, that the cuts are expected by the end of 2026 and into Q1 2027. Some cuts have already started in the games division (Paramount Games and Skydance Interactive), according to employee posts as of Nov 9, 2026, though Skydance has not confirmed them or given a number. This follows an earlier round: on Oct 29, 2025, after the Skydance–Paramount merger, Paramount began cutting about 2,000 jobs (roughly 10% of its workforce), starting with about 1,000 that day.

key_facts.fact: Ellison and Kreiz told employees that combining with Warner Bros. would involve layoffs. The company targets more than $6B in annual cost savings within three years and has not said how many jobs will be cut.
Paramount Skydance has begun layoffs in its games division (Paramount Games, Skydance Interactive), based on employee LinkedIn posts. Skydance has not disclosed a headcount or confirmed the cuts.
Variety reports that layoffs are expected by the end of 2026 and into Q1 2027, with no announced job count. The combined company's first quarterly report came out Nov 9, 2026.
On Oct 29, 2025, Paramount began laying off about 1,000 workers as part of about 2,000 cuts (about 10% of its workforce) after the Skydance merger.

passages.quote: Skydance has not disclosed how many people have lost their jobs or issued a statement confirming the cuts.
layoffs are expected by the end of 2026 and into the first quarter of 2027 (summarized from the page, citing Variety; not a verbatim quote)
Ellison's memo said the decisions are "never made lightly"; cuts are "part of that process" (about 2,000 employees, ~10% of workforce)

caveats: The Variety pieces on the Ellison/Kreiz memo and on voluntary buyouts plus a 5-day in-office policy were paywalled (HTTP 402). Their details come from secondary sources, and the exact date of the memo is unverified.
There is no official headcount for the 2026 merger-related layoffs. The games-division cuts are based on employee social-media posts and have not been confirmed by the company.
Secondary sources disagree on when the Warner Bros. Discovery deal closed: one search snippet says Nov 5, 2026, another says Oct 6, 2026. I could not confirm either.
Older layoff rounds (2024 under Paramount Global, Oct 2025 after the Skydance merger) often get mixed up with the 2026 cuts.
